types.embedding_query_text: PoliceForce: An organized body of people empowered by a state to enforce the law, protect property, and limit civil disorder. Also called LawEnforcementAgency, PoliceDepartment, Constabulary, Gendarmerie. Examples: Paris police.

chosen_type.label: PoliceForce
chosen_type.definition: An organized body of people empowered by a state to enforce the law, protect property, and limit civil disorder.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org candidate directly represents a police force as an organization; PoliceStation is a place, and other candidates are unrelated.

candidates.label: PoliceStation
candidates.comment: A PoliceStation is a CivicStructure serving as the headquarters for a local police force. Also called police department, precinct, law enforcement office. Examples: NYPD 10th Precinct, Scotland Yard, a local police headquarters, a sheriff's office.

candidates.label: LegalForceStatus
candidates.comment: LegalForceStatus is an enumeration of possible statuses for the legal force or validity of a legislation. Also called legal validity status, legislative effect, law status. Examples: 'InForce', 'Repealed', 'Expired', 'Pending'.

candidates.label: LegalService
candidates.comment: A LegalService is a local business that provides legally-oriented services, advice, and representation. Also called law firm, legal practice, attorney service. Examples: a corporate law firm, a family law attorney, a public defender's office.

candidates.label: GovernmentService
candidates.comment: A GovernmentService is an intangible service provided by a government organization to the public. Also called public service, state-provided service, municipal offering. Examples: food stamps program, veterans benefits, public education, waste collection.

candidates.label: DefenceEstablishment
candidates.comment: A government building or civic structure primarily used for military or national defense purposes. Also called Military base, army base, naval base, air force station. Examples: The Pentagon, Fort Bragg, Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard, Royal Air Force Lakenheath. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

types.embedding_query_text: Person: An individual human being. Also called Individual, Human, Citizen, Resident, Agent. Examples: man, Kheira Dellabed, young man with a small suitcase, waiter from a nearby restaurant.

chosen_type.label: Person
chosen_type.justification: schema.org's Person directly matches the OIE_TYPE and all mentions.

mentions: young man with a small suitcase

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: Residence
candidates.comment: A Residence is a Place where a person lives. Also called home, dwelling, abode. Examples: a house, an apartment, a condominium, a dormitory room.

candidates.label: IndividualPhysician
candidates.comment: An IndividualPhysician is a medical business representing a single medical practitioner. Also called doctor, medical doctor, general practitioner, specialist. Examples: Dr. Jane Smith (a family doctor), Dr. John Doe (a cardiologist), a local pediatrician. Distinct from Physician, which is the general role, and MedicalOrganization, which is a facility.

candidates.label: IndividualProduct
candidates.comment: An IndividualProduct is a single, identifiable instance of a product. Also called specific product unit, unique item, serialized product. Examples: a laptop with a specific serial number, a particular copy of a book, a unique piece of art. Distinct from ProductModel, which describes a class of products, and ProductGroup, which is a collection of products.

candidates.label: City
candidates.comment: A large and permanent human settlement, typically an administrative area with a defined government. Also called town, municipality, urban area, metropolis. Examples: New York City, London, Tokyo, Paris. Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a broader category including states, provinces, etc.

types.embedding_query_text: PersonGroup: A collection of two or more individuals. Also called GroupOfPeople, Crowd, Team, Party, Collective. Examples: three women, the three.

chosen_type.label: PersonGroup
chosen_type.definition: A collection of individuals sharing a common characteristic or involved in a common activity.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org candidate represents a general collection of people; PerformingGroup and MusicGroup are too specific, and Person is for individuals. Organization is the closest parent for a group of people.

candidates.label: PerformingGroup
candidates.comment: A PerformingGroup is an organization of performers, such as a band, orchestra, or circus. Also called performance ensemble, troupe, artistic group. Examples: Cirque du Soleil, a local theatre company, a dance troupe. Distinct from MusicGroup, which is specifically for musical performers.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: ProductGroup
candidates.comment: A ProductGroup is a Product representing a group of products that vary only in specific attributes like size, color, or material, serving as a template for its variants. Also called product family, product line, variant group. Examples: a specific model of smartphone available in different colors and storage sizes, a t-shirt design available in various sizes and fabrics, a car model with different trim levels. Distinct from Product, which is a specific variant offered for sale.

candidates.label: Taxon
candidates.comment: A cohesive biological unit representing a group of organisms, such as a species, genus, or family. Also called biological classification, taxonomic group, species, genus. Examples: Homo sapiens, Canis familiaris, Felidae (cat family), Plantae (plant kingdom).

candidates.label: MusicGroup
candidates.comment: A MusicGroup, as a PerformingGroup, is an organization of musicians, such as a band or orchestra, or a solo musician. Also called band, musical ensemble, orchestra, solo artist. Examples: The Beatles, New York Philharmonic, Taylor Swift. Distinct from PerformingGroup, which is a broader category for any performance group.

types.embedding_query_text: Weapon: An object or device used for fighting or for causing harm to others. Also called Armament, Implement, Tool, Instrument, Device. Examples: knives, two knives.

chosen_type.label: Weapon
chosen_type.definition: An object or device used for fighting or for causing harm to others.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org candidate directly represents a weapon; Product is too general, and other candidates are unrelated. Weapon can be considered a type of Product.

candidates.label: Product
candidates.comment: A Product is any offered good or service. Also called item, merchandise, offering. Examples: a pair of shoes, a concert ticket, a car rental service, an episode of a TV show.

candidates.label: Vehicle
candidates.comment: A device designed or used for transporting people or cargo across various environments. Also called conveyance, transport, automobile. Examples: a car, a bicycle, an airplane, a boat, a truck.

candidates.label: SportsEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

candidates.label: Drug
candidates.comment: A Drug is a Product that is a chemical or biological substance used as a medical therapy, having a physiological effect on an organism. Also called medicine, pharmaceutical, medication. Examples: Aspirin, Insulin, Penicillin, Ibuprofen.

candidates.label: SocialEvent
candidates.comment: An event primarily focused on social interaction and entertainment. Also called party, gathering, social function, get-together. Examples: a birthday party, a wedding reception, a community picnic, a networking mixer.

types.embedding_query_text: MedicalFacility: An institution providing medical and surgical treatment and nursing care for sick or injured people. Also called Hospital, Clinic, HealthcareCenter, Infirmary, Sanatorium. Examples: hospital.

chosen_type.label: MedicalFacility
chosen_type.definition: An institution providing medical and surgical treatment and nursing care for sick or injured people.
chosen_type.justification: MedicalClinic is too specific and explicitly distinct from a hospital, which is covered by the OIE_TYPE definition and mention. MedicalBusiness is the closest general parent for such an institution.

candidates.label: CovidTestingFacility
candidates.comment: A CovidTestingFacility is a medical clinic or other designated location where individuals can receive testing for the COVID-19 Coronavirus disease. Also called COVID test site, coronavirus testing center, SARS-CoV-2 testing facility. Examples: A drive-thru COVID testing center, a pharmacy offering COVID tests, a hospital's dedicated testing unit.

candidates.label: MedicalClinic
candidates.comment: A medical business facility, often associated with a hospital, dedicated to specific diagnosis and/or healthcare, typically for outpatients but sometimes inpatients. Also called clinic, healthcare center, medical facility. Examples: a dermatology clinic, a walk-in clinic, a university health clinic, a family practice. Distinct from Hospital, which is a larger institution providing comprehensive medical care.

candidates.label: MedicalRiskFactor
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing anything that increases a person's likelihood of developing a disease, medical condition, or complication. Also called risk element, predisposing factor, vulnerability. Examples: "smoking", "high cholesterol", "family history of heart disease", "obesity". Distinct from MedicalRiskEstimator, which is a tool to calculate risk based on multiple factors.

candidates.label: ParkingFacility
candidates.comment: A ParkingFacility is a civic structure providing space for parking vehicles. Also called parking lot, parking garage, car park. Examples: a multi-story parking garage, a supermarket parking lot, a valet parking service. Distinct from Road, which is for vehicle travel.

candidates.label: MedicalCause
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing the causative agent(s) responsible for a pathophysiologic process leading to a medical condition, symptom, or sign. Also called etiology, causative factor, underlying reason. Examples: "HIV virus" as a cause of AIDS, "pulmonary embolism" as a cause of cardiac arrest, "bacterial infection".

types.embedding_query_text: Time: A specific point or period in the sequence of events. Also called Moment, Hour, Period, Duration, Instant. Examples: 11:30 am (0930 GMT), around 11:30 am (0930 GMT).

chosen_type.label: Time
chosen_type.justification: schema.org's Time datatype perfectly matches the OIE_TYPE and mention of a specific clock time.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: InstantaneousEvent
candidates.comment: An InstantaneousEvent is a structured value representing an event with no duration, such as a single point in time. Also called momentary event, point event, discrete occurrence. Examples: a computer log entry, a timestamp, a single click on a webpage. Distinct from Event, which typically has a duration.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

types.embedding_query_text: District: A specific area of a city or country, often defined for administrative or geographical purposes. Also called Neighborhood, Borough, Region, Zone, Sector. Examples: Porte de Clichy area, northwest 17th district.

chosen_type.label: AdministrativeArea
chosen_type.justification: schema.org's AdministrativeArea is a suitable general category for a district, which is an administrative division.

candidates.label: City
candidates.comment: A large and permanent human settlement, typically an administrative area with a defined government. Also called town, municipality, urban area, metropolis. Examples: New York City, London, Tokyo, Paris. Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a broader category including states, provinces, etc.

candidates.label: AdministrativeArea
candidates.comment: An AdministrativeArea is a geographical region, typically governed by a specific authority. Also called political division, jurisdiction, governmental region, territory. Examples: A country, a state, a province, a city, a county.

candidates.label: DefinedRegion
candidates.comment: A geographic area defined by specific, potentially non-administrative criteria, such as a set of postal codes or states. Also called Custom region, service area, delivery zone, sales territory. Examples: "All US states except Alaska and Hawaii", "Postal codes 90210-90215", "The greater London area for delivery". Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a politically defined region like a state or county.

candidates.label: SchoolDistrict
candidates.comment: An administrative area responsible for the organization and operation of public schools within its geographical boundaries. Also called education district, school system, local education authority. Examples: 'Los Angeles Unified School District', 'New York City Department of Education', 'Springfield School District 186'.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

types.embedding_query_text: City: A large and densely populated urban area. Also called Metropolis, Town, UrbanCenter, Municipality, Capital. Examples: Paris, German capital of Berlin, the capital, the German capital of Berlin.

chosen_type.label: City
chosen_type.justification: schema.org's City directly matches the OIE_TYPE and mentions.

candidates.label: City
candidates.comment: A large and permanent human settlement, typically an administrative area with a defined government. Also called town, municipality, urban area, metropolis. Examples: New York City, London, Tokyo, Paris. Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a broader category including states, provinces, etc.

candidates.label: CityHall
candidates.comment: A government building serving as the administrative headquarters for a city or town. Also called town hall, municipal building, civic center. Examples: New York City Hall, London City Hall, a local town's municipal office. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: StadiumOrArena
candidates.comment: A large civic structure designed for sporting events, concerts, or other large-scale public gatherings. Also called stadium, arena, coliseum, sports complex. Examples: Wembley Stadium, Madison Square Garden, the Roman Colosseum.

candidates.label: ApartmentComplex
candidates.comment: An ApartmentComplex is a Residence consisting of a building or group of buildings containing multiple individual apartment units. Also called residential complex, flat complex, housing estate. Examples: The Grand Apartments, Sunset Towers, a student housing complex, a condominium development. Distinct from Apartment, which is a single housing unit within a complex.

types.embedding_query_text: GovernmentOfficial: A person holding an office in a government. Also called PublicServant, Statesperson, Minister, Bureaucrat, Administrator. Examples: Laurent Nunez, Geoffroy Boulard, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez, Nunez.

chosen_type.label: GovernmentOfficial
chosen_type.definition: A person holding an office in a government.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org candidate represents a person in a government role; all candidates are places, organizations, or services. Person is the appropriate parent.

candidates.label: GovernmentOffice
candidates.comment: A GovernmentOffice is a local business representing a specific governmental agency or department. Also called public agency office, state department branch, municipal service center. Examples: IRS office, DMV office, local planning department, social security office. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is the physical structure that may contain multiple offices.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: GovernmentService
candidates.comment: A GovernmentService is an intangible service provided by a government organization to the public. Also called public service, state-provided service, municipal offering. Examples: food stamps program, veterans benefits, public education, waste collection.

candidates.label: GovernmentOrganization
candidates.comment: A GovernmentOrganization is an organization or agency that is part of a governmental body. Also called public sector entity, state agency, governmental body. Examples: Department of Defense, Environmental Protection Agency, National Institutes of Health, local city council.

candidates.label: GovernmentBenefitsType
candidates.comment: GovernmentBenefitsType is an enumeration of various government benefits, particularly those related to supporting situations like COVID-19. Also called public assistance types, state aid categories, welfare program kinds. Examples: unemployment benefits, stimulus checks, housing assistance, food stamps.

types.embedding_query_text: SocialMediaPlatform: An online service or site that facilitates interaction and content sharing among users. Also called SocialNetwork, OnlinePlatform, DigitalCommunity, WebService, App. Examples: X.

chosen_type.label: SocialMediaPlatform
chosen_type.definition: An online service or site that allows users to create and share content or to participate in social networking.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org candidate directly represents a social media platform; SocialMediaPosting is content, and other candidates are too general or unrelated. Service is the closest parent for an online offering.

candidates.label: SocialMediaPosting
candidates.comment: A creative work published on a social media platform, such as a blog post, tweet, or Facebook update. Also called social post, microblog post, status update, online share. Examples: a tweet from a celebrity, a Facebook status update, a blog post on Medium, an Instagram caption.

candidates.label: DiscussionForumPosting
candidates.comment: A social media posting that is an entry or message within an online discussion forum. Also called Forum post, message board entry, thread reply, online discussion. Examples: A question posted on a tech support forum, a comment in a gaming community thread, a new topic started on a hobby board. Distinct from BlogPosting, which is typically a longer, standalone article on a blog.

candidates.label: RuntimePlatform
candidates.comment: A specialized software environment providing the necessary infrastructure, libraries, and services for executing a program. Also called execution environment, software platform, runtime environment, operating system. Examples: Java Virtual Machine (JVM), Node.js runtime, .NET Common Language Runtime (CLR), Python interpreter.

candidates.label: UserPlusOnes
candidates.comment: An outdated type representing a user's interaction of giving a "+1" endorsement, typically on Google+ or similar platforms. Also called user endorsement, +1, social recommendation. Examples: a user giving a +1 to a web page, endorsing a business, recommending content.

candidates.label: DigitalPlatformEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration listing common technology platforms, used to specify where an action or content is available. Also called Technology platform, software platform, operating system, device type. Examples: iOS, Android, Web, Desktop, Console. Distinct from SoftwareApplication, which is the application itself, not the platform it runs on.

types.embedding_query_text: PoliceOfficer: A warranted employee of a police force. Also called Officer, Constable, LawEnforcementOfficer, Patrolman, Detective. Examples: off-duty police officer, an off-duty police officer.

chosen_type.label: PoliceOfficer
chosen_type.definition: A warranted employee of a police force.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org candidate represents a police officer as a person; all candidates are places or business types. Person is the appropriate parent.

candidates.label: PoliceStation
candidates.comment: A PoliceStation is a CivicStructure serving as the headquarters for a local police force. Also called police department, precinct, law enforcement office. Examples: NYPD 10th Precinct, Scotland Yard, a local police headquarters, a sheriff's office.

candidates.label: GovernmentOffice
candidates.comment: A GovernmentOffice is a local business representing a specific governmental agency or department. Also called public agency office, state department branch, municipal service center. Examples: IRS office, DMV office, local planning department, social security office. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is the physical structure that may contain multiple offices.

candidates.label: PostOffice
candidates.comment: A PostOffice is a GovernmentOffice providing postal services. Also called postal service branch, mail office. Examples: USPS Post Office, Royal Mail sorting office, a local post office branch, a general post office.

candidates.label: ProfessionalService
candidates.comment: ProfessionalService is a LocalBusiness type for providers of specialized services. Also called expert service, specialized service. Examples: a legal service, an accounting service, a dental practice, an architectural firm. Distinct from Service, which is a broader concept of an intangible offering.

candidates.label: PhysiciansOffice
candidates.comment: A PhysiciansOffice, as a Physician, is a doctor's office or clinic where medical consultations and treatments are provided. Also called doctor's clinic, medical office, medical practice. Examples: a family doctor's practice, a specialist's clinic, an urgent care center. Distinct from Hospital, which offers inpatient care and emergency services.

types.embedding_query_text: Object: A material thing that can be seen and touched. Also called Item, Thing, Article, Device, Entity. Examples: bag, chair, his bag, a chair.

chosen_type.label: Thing
chosen_type.justification: schema.org's Thing is the most generic type and aligns with the broad definition of 'Object' as a material thing.

candidates.label: Thing
candidates.comment: The most generic and fundamental type in schema.org, representing any item or entity. Also called entity, item, object. Examples: a person, a book, a place, an event.

candidates.label: Vehicle
candidates.comment: A device designed or used for transporting people or cargo across various environments. Also called conveyance, transport, automobile. Examples: a car, a bicycle, an airplane, a boat, a truck.

candidates.label: Product
candidates.comment: A Product is any offered good or service. Also called item, merchandise, offering. Examples: a pair of shoes, a concert ticket, a car rental service, an episode of a TV show.

candidates.label: Class
candidates.comment: An intangible concept representing a category or type of entity, equivalent to rdfs:Class. Also called type, category, kind, schema. Examples: "Person" class, "Product" class, "Event" class. Distinct from DefinedTerm, which is a specific term within a vocabulary.

candidates.label: ImageObject
candidates.comment: An ImageObject is a media object creative work representing an image file. Also called picture, photo, graphic, visual. Examples: a JPEG photograph, a PNG illustration, a GIF animation. Distinct from VideoObject, which is a video file, and AudioObject, which is an audio file.

types.embedding_query_text: Date: A particular day, specified by number, month, and year. Also called Day, CalendarDate, SpecificDate, PointInTime, Epoch. Examples: Saturday, on Saturday.

chosen_type.label: DayOfWeek
chosen_type.justification: schema.org's DayOfWeek specifically represents a day of the week, which matches the mention 'Saturday', whereas Date is for a specific calendar date.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

types.embedding_query_text: Vehicle: A means of carrying or transporting something. Also called Conveyance, Transport, Automobile, Car, Truck. Examples: rented minivan, a rented minivan.

chosen_type.label: Vehicle
chosen_type.justification: schema.org's Vehicle directly matches the OIE_TYPE and the mention 'minivan' is a type of vehicle.

candidates.label: Vehicle
candidates.comment: A device designed or used for transporting people or cargo across various environments. Also called conveyance, transport, automobile. Examples: a car, a bicycle, an airplane, a boat, a truck.

candidates.label: Car
candidates.comment: A wheeled, self-powered motor vehicle primarily used for personal transportation. Also called automobile, motorcar, auto, vehicle. Examples: Toyota Camry, Ford F-150, Tesla Model 3, Honda Civic.

candidates.label: BusOrCoach
candidates.comment: A BusOrCoach is a Vehicle designed to carry multiple passengers, with coaches being luxury versions for long-distance travel. Also called omnibus, motorcoach, passenger bus, tour bus. Examples: city bus, Greyhound coach, school bus, double-decker bus.

candidates.label: MotorizedBicycle
candidates.comment: A vehicle that is primarily a bicycle equipped with an attached motor for power or assistance. Also called e-bike, electric bicycle, moped (older sense). Examples: a pedal-assist electric bicycle, a bicycle with a small gas engine kit. Distinct from Motorcycle, which is designed from the ground up as a motor vehicle.

candidates.label: Motorcycle
candidates.comment: A vehicle that is a single-track, two-wheeled motor vehicle. Also called motorbike, two-wheeler, scooter. Examples: a Harley-Davidson, a Honda CBR, a Vespa scooter. Distinct from MotorizedBicycle, which is primarily a bicycle with an assisting motor.

types.embedding_query_text: Event: A happening or occurrence, especially one of importance. Also called Incident, Occurrence, Happening, Affair, Circumstance. Examples: Pride parade, a Pride parade.

chosen_type.label: Event
chosen_type.justification: schema.org's Event directly matches the OIE_TYPE and the mention 'Pride parade' is an event.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: SportsEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

candidates.label: Festival
candidates.comment: A Festival is an Event that is a public celebration or series of special events. Also called celebration, gala, fete. Examples: A music festival, a film festival, a cultural heritage festival, a food and wine festival.

candidates.label: ConferenceEvent
candidates.comment: An event specifically organized as a conference, typically involving presentations, discussions, and networking. Also called conference, convention, symposium, summit. Examples: A tech conference, an academic symposium, a business summit, a medical convention. Distinct from Event, which is a general occurrence.

candidates.label: DeliveryEvent
candidates.comment: An event representing the delivery of an item, typically a product or package. Also called Shipping event, package delivery, consignment event. Examples: A package arriving at its destination, a food delivery being completed, a furniture delivery appointment. Distinct from Order, which is the request for items, not the delivery itself.

types.embedding_query_text: Quantity: A specific amount or number of something. Also called Amount, Number, Count, Volume, Measure. Examples: 29.

chosen_type.label: Quantity
chosen_type.justification: schema.org's Quantity datatype directly matches the OIE_TYPE and covers numerical values like '29'.

candidates.label: Quantity
candidates.comment: Quantity is a data type representing measurable amounts such as distance, time, mass, or weight. Also called amount, measure, magnitude. Examples: '3 kg', '4 milligrams', '10 meters', '2 hours'.

candidates.label: Mass
candidates.comment: A quantity representing the amount of matter in an object, typically expressed with a unit of measure. Also called weight, bulk, quantity of matter. candidates.label: Number
candidates.comment: Number is a data type representing numerical values. Also called numeric value, quantity, digit. Examples: 10, 3.14, -5, 1000000. Distinct from Text, which represents character strings.

candidates.label: Distance

candidates.label: Duration

candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: ServicePeriod
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a duration for a service, often including constraints like cutoff times or business days. Also called service duration, operational window, delivery timeframe, handling period. Examples: a 2-day shipping period with a 3 PM cutoff, a 5-business-day processing time, a 24/7 support period.

types.embedding_query_text: BodyPart: A distinct part of an animal or human body. Also called Organ, Limb, Anatomy, Structure, Member. Examples: lower back, abdomen.

chosen_type.label: AnatomicalStructure
chosen_type.justification: schema.org's AnatomicalStructure perfectly matches the OIE_TYPE and mentions like 'lower back' and 'abdomen'.

candidates.label: AnatomicalStructure
candidates.comment: An AnatomicalStructure is a MedicalEntity representing any part of the human body, such as organs, tissues, or cells. Also called body part, biological structure, anatomical component. Examples: The heart, a bone, a muscle, a neuron, the liver. Distinct from AnatomicalSystem, which is a group of structures working together.

candidates.label: AnatomicalSystem
candidates.comment: An AnatomicalSystem is a MedicalEntity comprising a group of anatomical structures that function together to perform a specific task. Also called organ system, biological system, body system. Examples: The circulatory system, the digestive system, the nervous system, the skeletal system. Distinct from AnatomicalStructure, which is an individual part of the body.

candidates.label: SuperficialAnatomy
candidates.comment: Anatomical features observable by sight without dissection, including body form, proportions, and surface landmarks corresponding to deeper structures. Also called surface anatomy, external anatomy, visible body structures. Examples: the visible edges of the scapula, the cubital fossa for vein location, the contours of muscles under the skin.

candidates.label: Bone
candidates.comment: An AnatomicalStructure consisting of rigid connective tissue that forms the skeletal structure of a body. Also called skeletal bone, osseous tissue. Examples: "Femur", "Skull bone", "Rib cage", "Vertebra". Distinct from Muscle, which is soft tissue for movement.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

types.embedding_query_text: Condition: The state of something with regard to its appearance, quality, or working order. Also called State, Status, Situation, Circumstance, Predicament. Examples: pregnant.

chosen_type.label: MedicalCondition
chosen_type.justification: schema.org's MedicalCondition is the best fit for 'pregnant', which is a state of the body.

candidates.label: MedicalCondition
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing any condition of the human body that affects normal functioning, including diseases, injuries, disabilities, and disorders. Also called disease, illness, health disorder, ailment. Examples: "influenza", "diabetes", "a broken arm", "depression", "asthma".

candidates.label: MedicalSignOrSymptom
candidates.comment: A medical condition representing any feature, objective or subjective, associated with a medical condition. Also called clinical manifestation, health indicator, disease feature. Examples: "pain", "fever", "fatigue", "rash", "nausea". Distinct from MedicalCondition, which is the underlying state itself.

candidates.label: StatusEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration type representing various status types or states. Also called status list, state types, condition enumeration. Examples: 'Active', 'Pending', 'Completed', 'Cancelled'.

candidates.label: OrderStatus
candidates.comment: OrderStatus is an enumeration for the status values of an Order. Also called order state, delivery status, fulfillment status. Examples: OrderProcessing, OrderDelivered, OrderCancelled, OrderProblem. Distinct from PaymentStatusType, which describes the payment's state.

candidates.label: OfferItemCondition
candidates.comment: OfferItemCondition is an enumeration listing possible conditions for an item being offered. Also called item state, product condition, quality status. Examples: NewCondition, UsedCondition, RefurbishedCondition, DamagedCondition. Distinct from OfferShippingDetails, which describes shipping logistics.
